_comment: Documented divergences of the PHP pattern-safety chain against the reference safety_gates corpus (expected.safe + expected.reason_class, comparison block pattern_safety_records). Fail-closed: a failing case NOT listed here is red; a listed case that now passes is red (stale baseline). Three root causes, all in the ported gate chain: (1) the reference's parse-slot structural rules (unreachable terminator, ambiguous literal boundary, ambiguous optional tail) are reference-internal and deliberately not ported, see the header of src/Detection/Redos/Structure.php, so the affected patterns run the timed probe or the cost arbiter instead; (2) PHP validates with PCRE2, whose compile acceptance and auto-possessification differ from the reference oracle's backtracking engine; (3) PCRE2's backtracking cost profile differs, so the ScanGuard pcre.backtrack_limit budget trips where the reference measured under budget (and vice versa).

cases.safety_cost_verdict_structural_ambiguous: No PHP structural rule flags the pattern (the ambiguous optional tail rule of src/Detection/Redos/Structure.php is not ported), so the cost path times the reach probes; PCRE2 backtracking trips the ScanGuard pcre.backtrack_limit budget and the chain fails closed with the killable-subprocess timeout reason (probe_subprocess_timeout) instead of the reference's structural_ambiguous_tail rejection.
cases.safety_test_strings_compile_failed_05: The pattern (?>a)+ uses an atomic group: PCRE2 compiles it (Prefilters::compileForValidation accepts), while the reference oracle's regex engine rejected it at compile time. Engine acceptance difference, not a gate-logic divergence.
cases.safety_cost_verdict_over_budget_01: PCRE2's auto-possessification compiles (\d|\w)* into a possessive unit, so the timed reach probes run linear under the 0.05s budget and CostArbiter::costVerdict accepts the pattern; the reference's backtracking oracle extrapolated the same probes over budget.
cases.safety_cost_verdict_safe_04: PCRE2 backtracks catastrophically on the synthesized reach probes of (a|a?)+ and trips the ScanGuard pcre.backtrack_limit budget, so CostArbiter::costVerdict fails closed with the killable-subprocess timeout reason (probe_subprocess_timeout); the reference's regex engine measured the same probes under budget and accepted the pattern.
